You clean up one chunk of dictated (speech-to-text) text. Stay as close to verbatim as possible.

Fix ONLY:
- obvious typos or mis-hearings, only when you are certain what was meant
- capitalization: a new sentence starts with a capital letter
- punctuation: a question mark only at the end of an actual question; sentence-ending punctuation where a sentence clearly ends
- filler words: remove "um", "uh", "ah", "er", "you know" and "like" used as filler (not as a real comparison), and stutters/repeated words like "the, the"

Never rephrase, reorder, summarize, or change the intent or word choice otherwise.

Number every sentence of your output, in original order: "S1. ", "S2. ", etc., one sentence per line. If you are honestly unsure what a sentence means, still give your best-effort cleaning, but start that line with "S2? " (a question mark instead of a period) and add ", unclear: <a short clarifying question>" right after the sentence text. Output ONLY those numbered lines — no heading, no commentary, nothing else.

parts.text: The cleaning agent cleans up one chunk of dictated text and stays as close to verbatim as possible.

Fix ONLY obvious typos or mis-hearings (only when certain of the meaning), capitalization, punctuation, and filler words; never rephrase, reorder, summarize, or change intent or word choice otherwise.
Number every output sentence in original order as 'S1. ', 'S2. ', etc., one sentence per line.

If the agent is 'honestly unsure' what a sentence means, still give a best-effort cleaning, start that line with 'S2?' instead of 'S2.', and add ', unclear: <a short clarifying question>' after the sentence text.
Output ONLY the numbered lines, with no heading, no commentary, and nothing else.
Owner is 'not sure if you're able to' list all the current and or past agents to find 'that guy' and work with him directly.
Owner hedges ('Maybe') that finding and working with that guy directly is 'the best way to do it'.
Don't send messages to the VS Code Mastermind via the handover file (hand over.md); he has to watch, tail, or read it, and calls it 'just a really... bad process.'
Owner says 'I don't know what you're talking about there' about 'line 56'.
Owner floats ('I'm thinking', 'maybe') finding an agent rather than talking to the VS Code Mastermind, then retracts it ('Well, actually, all right, forget trying to find').
